_meta.purpose: Atomic fragments of a multi-step flow, captured 1:1 from the catalog block frames. patterns.json composes them via $ref.
_meta.spacingModel: The stepper row and the nav row both SPAN the content column and push their ends apart (spread) — measured on the templates: the stepper's four items sit at 0/310/619/940 of 1024 (gaps 230) and the nav's Ghost/Brand buttons at 0 and 941. Neither row is hug and neither is packed left; a fixed gap is a capture error. A step's heading pair is one block at lg. The step content column separates its blocks at xl.
_meta.stateModel: One rendered frame = ONE step. The stepper distinguishes THREE item states, per template 1716:21928: DONE carries the `check` icon plus the label, ACTIVE carries the `pen` icon plus the label in strong text, and PENDING is a muted label PREFIXED WITH ITS STEP NUMBER ("3. Fahrbereitschaft"). Exactly one item is active — the step the frame shows. Never render every item in the pending shape: without an icon the row reads as plain text and the stepper is not recognizable as progress. Prototyping is out of scope: deliver each step as its own static frame.
_meta.placeholders: <Angle brackets> mark content the agent MUST replace. <Trailing?> marks an optional node: drop it when no content applies, never render it empty.

process.stepper-step-done.purpose: Completed stepper item: check icon plus the step name.

process.stepper-step-active.purpose: The step the frame currently shows: pen icon plus the step name in strong text. Exactly one stepper item uses this shape.

process.stepper-step.purpose: Pending stepper item: the step NUMBER plus the step name, muted and without an icon. The number is what distinguishes a not-yet-reached step from the active one.

process.stepper.purpose: Horizontal stepper spanning the content column: completed steps, then the ACTIVE step, then the numbered pending ones. The row is spread — the items mark progress across the full width, so the template distributes them edge to edge (0/310/619/940 of 1024) instead of packing them left at a fixed gap.

process.progress.purpose: Counter line above a determinate progress bar.

process.step-title.purpose: Step heading pair: h2 title with an optional large description.

process.navigation-first.purpose: Step navigation for the FIRST step, where there is nothing to go back to: a single right-aligned Brand action. Deliberately NOT `spread: true` — SPACE_BETWEEN needs two ends, and with one child Figma parks it flush LEFT with the whole content column empty to its right. One action belongs right.

process.navigation.purpose: Step navigation SPANNING the content column: Back as ghost on the left edge, Next as the Brand action on the right edge. The template pushes them apart (buttons at 0 and 941 of 1024) — a hug row that packs both buttons together on the left is a capture error. On the FIRST step, where `Zurück` is dropped, use process.navigation-first instead: a single action is right-aligned, not spread.

process.success.purpose: Confirmation content: check-circle icon, centered h1, description and one action.
